indicators.name: Unemployment rate
indicators.description: Share of the labor force that is jobless and actively looking for work (U-3, seasonally adjusted).

indicators.name: Real GDP growth
indicators.description: Quarter-over-quarter change in inflation-adjusted GDP, expressed at an annual rate. Noisy by nature; look at the shape, not single quarters.

indicators.name: Inflation (CPI, year over year)
indicators.description: Percent change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers versus the same month a year earlier.

indicators.name: Labor force participation
indicators.description: Share of the civilian population aged 16+ that is working or looking for work. Strongly shaped by demographics (baby-boomer retirement), not just policy.

indicators.name: Real median weekly earnings (1982–84 $)
indicators.description: Median usual weekly earnings of full-time wage and salary workers, adjusted for inflation (CPI-U, 1982–84 dollars).

indicators.name: Real median household income
indicators.description: Median household income adjusted for inflation to the most recent year's dollars (Census CPS ASEC). Published once a year, about nine months after the year ends.

indicators.name: Poverty rate
indicators.description: Estimated share of people of all ages living in poverty (Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates). Starts in 1989.

indicators.name: Federal surplus or deficit (% of GDP)
indicators.description: Federal budget balance by fiscal year as a share of GDP. Negative is a deficit. Budgets are set by Congress; the president proposes and signs.

indicators.name: Federal debt (% of GDP)

source.publisher: Office of Management and Budget / Fed. Reserve Bank of St. Louis
source.label: FRED GFDEGDQ188S

indicators.description: Total public debt (including debt held by federal trust funds) as a share of GDP.

indicators.name: Violent crime rate
indicators.description: Murders, rapes, robberies and aggravated assaults reported to police, per 100,000 people (FBI national estimates). Estimates from 2021 on are based on the FBI's new incident-based system (NIBRS) and aren't strictly comparable with earlier years.

indicators.name: Property crime rate
indicators.description: Burglaries, larcenies and motor vehicle thefts reported to police, per 100,000 people (FBI national estimates). Estimates from 2021 on are based on the FBI's new incident-based system (NIBRS) and aren't strictly comparable with earlier years.

indicators.name: Murder rate
indicators.description: Murders and non-negligent manslaughters per 100,000 people (FBI national estimates). The 2001 figure excludes the deaths of September 11. Estimates from 2021 on are based on the FBI's new incident-based system (NIBRS) and aren't strictly comparable with earlier years.

indicators.name: Firearm death rate

source.publisher: CDC National Center for Health Statistics
source.label: CDC WONDER

indicators.description: Deaths from firearm injuries of any intent (suicide, homicide, accident), age-adjusted, per 100,000 people. From death certificates; final data starts in 1999. Roughly half are suicides. Points after the last final year are provisional rolling 12-month rates from the CDC's quarterly estimates, shown dashed.

indicators.name: Life expectancy at birth
indicators.description: Years a newborn would live if current mortality patterns held. Driven by medicine, behavior and shocks (opioids, COVID) over long horizons.

indicators.name: Drug overdose death rate

where.estimate_type: Deaths per 100,000 resident population, age adjusted

source.publisher: CDC National Center for Health Statistics
source.label: data.cdc.gov

indicators.description: Drug overdose deaths per 100,000 people, age-adjusted. Two CDC datasets joined at 2018, where both report the same value. Final data starts in 1999. Points after the last final year are provisional rolling 12-month rates from the CDC's quarterly estimates, shown dashed.

indicators.name: Uninsured rate
indicators.description: Share of the civilian population with no health insurance at the time of the survey (ACS). Starts in 2008; there is no 2020 value because the pandemic disrupted that year's survey. The ACA's main coverage provisions began in 2014.
